learning_objective: 🎯 Master the foundation of all sports: Athletics and Gymnastics! Learn the rules, track measurements, and techniques of individual excellence.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Athletics is known as the 'mother of all sports'. It consists of running, jumping, and throwing. It is divided into Track Events (runs) and Field Events (jumps and throws).
Includes Sprints (100m, 200m, 400m), Middle Distance (800m, 1500m), Long Distance (5000m, 10000m), and Relays. Speed, reaction time, and stamina are key.
Jumps include Long Jump, High Jump, and Triple Jump. Throws include Shot Put, Discus, Javelin, and Hammer throw. They require explosive power and perfect technique.
A sport involving performance of exercises requiring physical strength, flexibility, power, agility, coordination, and balance (e.g., floor exercise, vault, balance beam).
A standard athletic track is 400 meters long, usually with 8 lanes. Knowing lane staggers (starting positions) is crucial for fair races.

fun_activity.title: 🐸 Standing Broad Jump Test
fun_activity.instructions: Mark a line on the ground. Stand behind it with feet together, bend your knees, swing your arms, and jump as far forward as you can. Use a measuring tape to see your distance!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the standard length of an athletic track (400m) and standard lane width (1.22m).
📌 Know the difference between Sprinting (requires explosive speed) and Long Distance (requires endurance).
📌 Learn the basic phases of a jump: Approach run, Take-off, Flight, and Landing.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Baton is used in Relay races and must be passed within the exchange zone.
⭐ Shot put requires athletes to 'put' (push) a heavy metal ball rather than throw it.
⭐ Gymnastics builds foundational motor skills useful for every other sport.
